statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The weekend venue closure leaves no live Nasdaq-100 price path to observe, so Tail remains far below the block threshold, while Stress stays elevated on hawkish rate repricing and an unresolved US-Iran tanker exchange around the Strait of Hormuz.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the whole outlook; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: No live Nasdaq-100 price path into a thin 22:00 UTC reopen, with OPEC+ on hold and the US-Iran tanker exchange unresolved before a US Labor Day holiday
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: ^NDX closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, and VIX ended at 14.53 after a 13.80-14.58 day range. No new market-moving development has been verified in the hour since the previous assessment; the two Sunday items already in evidence remain the OPEC+ decision and Iranian escalation rhetoric. Key OPEC+ members including Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman held October output policy unchanged at an online meeting, ending six consecutive monthly increases and scheduling the next meeting for October 4; reporting notes the group has limited influence over the physical market while Hormuz flows are disrupted. Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said further attacks would meet a faster, heavier and more painful response. The underlying escalation is unchanged: US Central Command reported three Iranian crude tankers permanently disabled or destroyed on September 5 after Iranian ballistic missiles were fired toward a US carrier and destroyer, and the IRGC said it targeted three tankers plus three US-linked vessels. Brent settled Friday at 96.28 dollars, more than 8 percent higher on the week and its highest since July 24, with reported Hormuz transits near 13 vessels per day against more than 100 before the conflict. The rates backdrop is unchanged: the BLS Employment Situation for August printed 162,000 payrolls against a consensus near 53,000 with unemployment steady at 4.1 percent, lifting implied odds of a 25bp hike at the September 15-16 FOMC to roughly 62 percent, and H.15 still shows the September 3 readings of 2Y 4.34 percent and 10Y 4.77 percent. The pre-FOMC communications blackout began September 5 and runs through September 17. Shared delayed cross-asset context refreshed at 14:26 UTC and is within its freshness threshold, but it is explicitly latest-session and non-real-time, so it confirms rather than replaces the absent price path; on that basis Friday megacaps were 3 up and 5 down with a -1.22 percent mean while all seven tracked semiconductors were higher, a directionally mixed picture that reduces conviction rather than amplifying Tail. Because no live price path exists, no directional efficiency, shallow-pullback sequence or failed retracement can be observed, so Tail is held in the low band at 5 and the conditional risk is placed in the 22:00 UTC reopen hour, where two closed days of unresolved escalation would be absorbed by the thinnest order book of the week. Stress stays elevated at 57 on the unresolved rates and energy backdrop. US cash equity markets are closed on Monday September 7 for Labor Day, so no US cash open falls inside this outlook; the next verified checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held flat at 4-5 with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress rose from 42 during Saturday's European afternoon to 57 around the Saturday evening tanker exchange, then oscillated between 52 and 57 across the remaining weekend closure and finished the window at 57. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover eight further closed hours, the scheduled 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday with no US cash open inside the window. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band except for the single reopen hour, which reaches 21 and maps to WATCH where an unresolved Hormuz tanker exchange and fresh Iranian escalation rhetoric would meet the thinnest depth of the week, before decaying toward 8 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 68 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop before unwinding toward 55. No US macro release falls inside the window, US cash equities and the Treasury market are closed on September 7 for Labor Day and the Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout; the next scheduled checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC.
